citeAs: Lu, P., Mishra, S., Xia, T., Qiu, L., Chang, K.-W., Zhu, S.-C., Tafjord, O., Clark, P., & Kalyan, A. (2022). Learn to Explain: Multimodal Reasoning via Thought Chains for Science Question Answering. NeurIPS 2022.
creator: Pan Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Tony Xia, Liang Qiu, Kai-Wei Chang, Song-Chun Zhu (University of California, Los Angeles); Oyvind Tafjord, Peter Clark, Ashwin Kalyan (Allen Institute for AI); Swaroop Mishra (Arizona State University)
description: SCIENCE QA is a multimodal multiple-choice science question dataset containing 21,208 examples from elementary and high school science curricula. Each example can include question text, image and/or text context, answer options, the correct answer, and in most cases grounded lectures and explanations spanning natural science, social science, and language science.
name: Science Question Answering (SCIENCE QA)
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions were downloaded from IXL learning resources and individual components such as questions, hints, images, options, answers, lectures, and solutions were extracted using heuristic rules. Invalid or duplicate questions were manually removed, answer options were shuffled, lectures and solutions were reformatted with semi-automated scripts, and incorrect annotations were further manually revised by experts using a data exploration tool.
rai:dataBiases: The paper notes the dataset is sourced from IXL Learning resources aligned with California Common Core Content Standards, which may bias content toward that curriculum and grade-school educational framing. The authors also state they examined the dataset for improper content and harmful social bias and would remove antisocial data points based on feedback.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected from open resources managed by IXL Learning, an online learning platform curated by K-12 education experts. The authors downloaded original science problems, extracted components including questions, hints, images, options, answers, lectures, and solutions using heuristic rules, manually filtered invalid and duplicate items, shuffled answer options, reformatted lectures and solutions with semi-automated scripts, and manually revised incorrect annotations with expert review.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Original science problems sourced from IXL Learning open resources, including questions, hints, images, options, answers, lectures, and solutions aligned with California Common Core Content Standards.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset remains challenging because models often fail to understand multimodal inputs, especially when image captions lack fine-grained semantics or do not work well for diagrams. The paper also notes errors arising from lack of domain-specific knowledge and generation of irrelevant, incorrect, or incomplete explanations.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: After collection, the authors manually removed invalid, faulty, and duplicate questions; kept only one correct answer when multiple answers applied; shuffled answer options; and reformatted lectures and solutions with semi-automated scripts to make structures such as tables and lists distinguishable.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Individual components were extracted from downloaded science problems using heuristic rules. The authors manually removed invalid questions, faulty data, and duplicates, retained one correct answer when multiple correct answers applied, shuffled answer options, and used semi-automated scripts to reformat lectures and solutions for easier use.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper states SCIENCE QA is intended to support multimodal understanding and multi-hop reasoning research and may benefit K-12 education applications such as tutoring systems. The authors report that the dataset does not contain user usage data or personally sensitive information such as gender and race, and that they did not find improper content, pornography, racial remarks, or harmful social bias; they would remove antisocial data points based on feedback.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is proposed as a benchmark for multimodal learning, multi-hop reasoning, scientific question answering, and general AI research. The paper also highlights potential use in K-12 education applications such as tutoring systems.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Heuristic rules and semi-automated scripts were used to extract and reformat questions, hints, images, options, answers, lectures, and solutions from the source problems.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The paper states the dataset does not contain user usage data or personally sensitive information such as gender and race, and does not contain personally identifiable information or offensive content.
